title: Zephyrine and the Cover
premise: Ulyana Thornbury discovers the safe house she's guarded for three years has been listed online, its interior photographed down to the hidden documents in the walls — proof that someone inside her own security firm sold them out. As three governments converge on the property and an assassin named Vess closes in, Ulyana realizes the 'clients nobody trusts' were never the target; she was, because she unknowingly memorized a decryption key during a routine drill. To survive, she must smuggle the truth to a journalist through hostile territory while deciding whether the firm that made her is worth saving. In the end, she burns her own identity to expose the conspiracy, walking away nameless but finally belonging to herself.
about_author: August Galloway is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for people who preferred their secrets kept. Galloway now writes thrillers from a coastal town whose location, fittingly, remains undisclosed.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. During a routine rotation at the Marlowe safe house, she finds the property listed for sale online — twelve photos of rooms only four living people have ever seen. Her stomach drops as she recognizes the angle of one shot: taken from inside her own bedroom. Emotional beat: violated calm, the first crack of paranoia.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reports the listing to her firm, Halcyon Detail, and is told to stand down and rotate out early — an order that makes no operational sense. She photographs everything before leaving anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to curdle into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Client POV (Elias Renner, a sanctioned financier). Renner summons Ulyana privately, convinced the listing means someone wants him findable. He hints he knows what was hidden in the safe house walls. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Twelve Photographs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Forensic review of the photos reveals they were taken over months — meaning the mole had long-term access. One image shows a wall panel Ulyana opened exactly once, during a training drill. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Assassin POV. The killer Vess receives a contract: retrieve the key from the former guard, leave no witnesses. We see his methodical professionalism and his one eccentricity — he collects his targets' identification cards. Emotional beat: cold menace, humanized just enough to unsettle.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Halcyon suspends her pending 'internal review,' freezing her accounts and revoking her credentials. She realizes the firm isn't investigating the leak; it's containing her. Emotional beat: betrayal, the ground giving way beneath identity built on rules.

chapters.title: What the Walls Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback interleaved with present. She reconstructs the drill where she opened the panel and recites, from memory, the alphanumeric string she was ordered to forget. It matches nothing she was told — it's a decryption key for a government slush ledger. Emotional beat: horrified understanding.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs — a liaison in London, an intelligence officer in Washington, a ministry fixer in Berlin — all quietly mobilizing toward the same question: who has the key? Emotional beat: converging pressure, the world tightening around one woman.

chapters.title: Renner's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Renner meet in a Rotterdam hotel bar. He offers protection and passage in exchange for exclusive use of the decrypted ledger — leverage, not truth. She refuses to hand it over whole. Emotional beat: temptation versus integrity.

chapters.title: The Card Collector
chapters.summary: Vess POV. He eliminates a Halcyon middleman and acquires Ulyana's file, learning her real name — which even she barely uses anymore. He begins anticipating her rather than hunting her. Emotional beat: intimacy of predation.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Ulyana returns covertly to the abandoned Marlowe house to verify the panel and finds evidence someone else got there first — and left a message for her: a single playing card, the zephyr. Emotional beat: being known by your enemy, terror sharpened into focus.

chapters.title: The Journalist Option
chapters.summary: Ulyana contacts Marguerite Osei, an investigative reporter with a history of surviving her sources. They agree on a dead-drop protocol, but Osei warns her: once published, there's no undoing it, for anyone. Emotional beat: commitment, point of no return approached.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: Firm director Corin Ashe's POV. Ashe explains — to himself, chillingly reasonably — why Ulyana must be discredited: the ledger implicates clients Halcyon cannot afford to lose. Power rationalizing corruption. Emotional beat: banality of institutional evil.

chapters.title: Run Light
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She goes dark, moving through Antwerp on cash and borrowed identities, testing which of her old contacts still answer. Most don't. One does — a retired trainer who owes her. Emotional beat: loneliness, the cost of belonging to no one.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Exchange
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The first dead-drop is compromised; Vess anticipated it. A brutal close-quarters escape leaves her wounded and Osei's photographer dead. Emotional beat: grief and fury, failure with teeth.

chapters.title: Renner's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Renner POV. Cornered by two governments, Renner sells Ulyana's route to buy his own immunity — then hesitates when he realizes he's delivering her to Vess, not to a court. Emotional beat: self-interest colliding with a conscience he didn't know he had.

chapters.title: The Zephyr Gambit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Instead of running, she uses the card message: she arranges to meet Vess on her terms, offering the key in exchange for the name of whoever contracted him. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into audacity.

chapters.title: Two Professionals
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana/Vess POV. In a shuttered canal warehouse, they negotiate like mirror images. Vess reveals his client is inside Halcyon itself — and that his contract changed: not retrieval now, but silence. Emotional beat: mutual recognition between hunter and prey.

chapters.title: Ashe's House of Cards
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Ulyana feeds Ashe fabricated proof that Vess is turning witness, forcing Halcyon to burn its own channels trying to contain him. The firm tears itself apart in forty-eight hours. Emotional beat: turning power's machinery against itself.

chapters.title: Ledger Night
chapters.summary: Climax part two. With governments closing in, Ulyana delivers the full decrypted ledger to Osei under conditions of maximum chaos — while Vess, contract voided by Halcyon's collapse, chooses to walk away rather than kill her, leaving her ID card on the table as a strange courtesy. Emotional beat: catharsis, survival against every odd.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The story breaks across three countries in one morning; resignations cascade, prosecutions begin, and Halcyon dissolves. Renner testifies to save himself. Ulyana watches from nowhere in particular, uncredited. Emotional beat: vindication without applause.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, living under no alias for the first time in years, she trains new security contractors — teaching them the rules, and when to break them. She keeps Vess's returned card in her pocket, a reminder of who she chose to be. Emotional beat: quiet resolution, belonging found within.
